Whether some are praiseworthy through confession, as in Judah; distinguished by the offspring of works, as in Reuben; strong in the exercise of temptations, as in Gad; blessed by victory in contests, as in Asher; enlarged through abundant works of mercy, as in Naphtali; forgetful of what lies behind, as in Manasseh; still sorrowful, as in Simeon, in the valley of tears, yet always rejoicing in the name of the dwelling place and longing for the heavenly Jerusalem; whether in Levi they rejoice together in the promises of the present and future life, established in eternal good through added temporal goods; whether in Issachar they are strengthened by contemplation of the future reward; whether in Zebulun they lay down their lives for Christ; whether in Joseph they strive both for an increase of spiritual substance and to offer something beyond God’s commandments, either in virginity or in the amount of their possessions; or whether in Benjamin they await the right hand of eternal blessedness with tireless prayers—in each person’s profession it is fitting that he be marked by the rule of the preceding fathers, as by the number twelve, and that from the merits of individual persons the most perfect beauty of the Church be gathered, as the sum of one hundred forty-four thousand.

**After this I saw a great multitude, which no one could count.** Having completed the recapitulation that he had inserted by way of example, he returns to the sequence, proclaiming the glory of those who will overcome the wickedness of the final persecution. And what follows:

[Col. 0152D] **From every nation, and tribe, and people, and language, etc.,** may also be understood in this way: after enumerating the tribes of Israel, to whom the Gospel was first preached, he also wishes to commemorate the salvation of the nations.

**Clothed in white robes, and with palms in their hands.** By the robes he indicates baptism; by the palms, the triumph of the cross and the fact that they have conquered the world in Christ. The robes may also signify the brightness bestowed through the Holy Spirit.

**And they cried out with a loud voice, saying: Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.** With a loud voice—that is, with profound devotion and unceasing praise—they confess that the Father and the Son reign upon the throne, that is, in the Church, while the Holy Spirit reigns with them. Thus it is said: “To him who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb” (Rev. V), just as the Gospel says: “That they may know you, the true and only God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent” (John XVII). The implied meaning is: “That they may know the one true God.”

**And all the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the living creatures.** In the collective body of the angels he explained the persons of the great multitude worshiping the Lord. “All,” he says, “who are around him will offer gifts” (Ps. LXXV).

**And they fell upon their faces before the throne, etc.** In this passage he does not say that the multitude, the living creatures, or the elders worshiped, but only the angels. For they themselves are the multitude; they themselves are the living creatures and the elders. Nevertheless, this may also be understood of the angelic spirits themselves, who rejoice together at the salvation of the nations, concerning whom it is said: “Rejoice, nations, with his people, and let all the angels of God worship him” (Rom. XV).

**Blessing and glory and wisdom, etc.** The Church offers the Lord a sevenfold praise of virtues, confessing that it has received them from him in its individual members.

**And one of the elders said to me: These who are clothed in white robes—who are they? etc.** He asks this in order to teach.

**And he said to me: These are they who came out of the great tribulation.** “Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God” (Acts XIV). Who, moreover, does not know that the tribulation of Antichrist will be greater than all others?

**And they washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.** He is not speaking only of the martyrs. They are washed in their own blood. But the entire Church is cleansed from every sin by the blood of Jesus, the Son of God (2 Cor. VII); therefore they are before God’s throne. Those are considered worthy to stand there in God’s service who here, amid adversity, remain faithful confessors of his name.

**And they serve him day and night in his temple.** Speaking in our customary manner, he signifies eternity.

**And he who sits upon the throne will dwell over them.** God’s throne is the saints, over and within whom God dwells forever.

**They will hunger no more, nor thirst any more.** This is what the Lord himself promised: “I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst” (John VI). “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied” (Matt. V).

**Neither will the sun fall upon them, nor any heat.** “We passed through fire and water,” he says, “and you brought us into refreshment” (Ps. LXV).

**For the Lamb, who is in the midst of the throne, will shepherd them.** He says that the Lamb is in the midst of the throne—the Lamb whom he had earlier said received the book from the one seated upon the throne—teaching that the Father and the Son have one throne, namely, the Church, in which through faith the one God, the whole Trinity, dwells.

**And he will lead them to the fountains of the waters of life.** That is, to fellowship with the saints, who are fountains of heavenly teaching. The very vision of God may also be signified, in whom the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden. As David says: “As the deer longs for the fountains of waters, so my soul longs for you, O God” (Ps. XLI).

**And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.** Having attained the fullness of immortal joys, every sorrow will be consigned to complete oblivion. “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.” The vision of this robed multitude may also be understood of the present time, in which we have been saved in hope and await with patience what we do not see.

## CHAPTER VIII

**And when he had opened the seventh seal, etc.** After the destruction of Antichrist, a brief period of rest is believed to await the Church, concerning which Daniel foretold: “Blessed is the one who waits and reaches the thousand three hundred thirty-five days” (Dan. XII). Blessed Jerome explains this as follows: “Blessed,” he says, “is the one who, after Antichrist has been killed, waits beyond the one thousand two hundred ninety days—that is, three and a half years—forty-five days, during which the Lord and Savior will come in his majesty.” Why there should be a silence of forty-five days after Antichrist’s death belongs to divine knowledge. Unless perhaps we say that the delay of the saints’ kingdom is a test of patience.

Note that in the sixth seal he sees the Church’s greatest tribulations, and in the seventh, rest, because the Lord, crucified on the sixth day, rested on the Sabbath, awaiting the time of resurrection. Thus far he has spoken of the opening of the sealed book and of the six seals. Now, however, he recapitulates from the beginning, intending to say the same things in another way.

## BOOK TWO

[Col. 0153]

[Col. 0153D] **And I saw seven angels standing in the presence of God, etc.** The Church, often commended by the number seven, is devoted to the ministry of preaching. Its first trumpet signifies the common destruction of the impious in fire and hail; the second, the devil driven from the Church and setting the sea of the world ablaze more fiercely; the third, heretics falling away from the Church and corrupting the rivers of Holy Scripture; the fourth, the decline of false brothers, represented by the darkening of the stars; the fifth, the greater infestation of heretics who precede the time of Antichrist; the sixth, the open war of Antichrist and his followers against the Church, together with the destruction of that adversary inserted in a recapitulation from the Lord’s advent; and the seventh, the day of judgment, when the Lord will repay his own and destroy those who corrupted the earth.

**And another angel came.** He did not say, “Afterward he came,” but, having proposed that the angels received the trumpets, he returns to explain how they received them. For although the Church preached before the Lord’s advent, it did not preach everywhere until it had been strengthened by his Spirit.

**And he stood before the altar, having a golden censer.** He appeared, that is, in the sight of the Church, himself having become the censer from which God received a sweet fragrance and was made propitious to the world. Another edition has “upon the altar,” meaning that upon the altar of the cross he offered his golden censer—that is, his immaculate body, conceived by the Holy Spirit—to the Father on our behalf.

**And much incense was given to him, etc.** He offered incense from the prayers of the saints. For the Church entrusted its prayers to him, saying: “Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight” (Ps. CXL). He is said both to have received the prayers of the saints and to have offered them because through him the prayers of all can reach God pleasantly.

**And the smoke of the incense ascended from the prayers of the saints, etc.** When Christ the Lord offered himself as an acceptable sacrifice, the contrition of the saints’ hearts became pleasing. Arising from an inner fire, it stirs tears as smoke ordinarily does.

**And the angel took the censer, etc.** Appropriately he introduces the censer as filled with fire. For God does not give the Spirit by measure (John III). We know that this was fulfilled especially in Christ’s humanity, in whom “the whole fullness of divinity dwells bodily” (Col. II).

**And he cast it upon the earth.** Thus also the Lord says in the Gospel: “I have come to cast fire upon the earth” (Luke XII).

**And there were thunderclaps, and voices, and flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.** With the thunder of heavenly warning, the voice of exhortation, and the flash of miracles, he moved the earth. Some pursued and others followed, some saying, “He is good,” but others, “No, he deceives the crowds” (John VII).

**And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound the trumpet.** The Church, inflamed by the sevenfold Spirit, confidently prepared itself for preaching, intending through the heavenly trumpets to cast down the glory of the world like the walls of Jericho. The circuit made over seven days likewise signifies the whole period of the Church.

**And the first angel sounded his trumpet.** The preaching of the trumpet’s plagues, which is a sign of war, is rightly compared to a trumpet. “Raise your voice,” he says, “like a trumpet, and announce their sins to my people” (Isa. LVIII). And elsewhere: “Let there be a trumpet in your throat, like an eagle over the house of the Lord” (Hos. VIII)—that is, preach in a loud voice that Nebuchadnezzar is coming for the destruction of the temple.

**And hail and fire came about, mixed with blood, etc.** The voice of the preachers reports that the punishment of hell is owed to bloody deeds, saying: “From excessive heat they will pass over from the waters of snow” (Job XXIV). The name “blood” may also be understood as signifying spiritual death itself. Tychonius explains this verse in the following way: “There came about the wrath of God, which contained the death of many.”

**And a third of the earth was burned, etc.** The life of the good consists in teachers and hearers. “Blessed is the one who reads,” he says, “and the one who hears the words of the prophecy” (Rev. I). The third part, namely, the wicked, lacks both. For the good earth, producing fruit in patience (Luke VIII), receives blessing from the Lord (Ps. XXIII). But the bad earth produces thorns and thistles, whose end is burning. Thus also the Father, the farmer, cultivates the fruitful tree, but cuts down the barren one and supplies fuel for the fire (Matt. VII).

**And all the green grass was burned.** “All flesh is grass” (Isa. XL). Now fattened by the softness of luxury, when the sun of judgment burns, it loses the flower of its beauty and, as the Lord says, “today is in the field, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven” (Matt. VI). Tychonius says of the third part at this point: “He calls internal enemies the third.” Otherwise, whatever is outside the Church is called the third part, and the Church is the third part that fights against the twofold evil.

**And something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea, etc.** As Christian religion increased, the devil, swollen with pride and burning with the fire of his fury, was cast into the sea of the world, as the Lord says: “If you say to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it will happen” (Mark XI). This does not mean that he had not been there previously, but that, having been cast out of the Church, he began to rage more fiercely against his own, inflicting spiritual death upon them through the arrogance of carnal wisdom. “To think according to the flesh is death” (Rom. VIII). Flesh and blood did not teach the apostles, but the Father who is in heaven (Matt. XVI). In that sea they guided the ship of faith, which offered itself to be trodden under the Lord’s feet.

**And a third of those creatures in the sea that had souls died.** He said “that had souls” in order to show that those who were spiritually alive had died. Thus the Apostle says of the pleasure-loving widow: “While living, she is dead” (1 Tim. V).

**And a third of the ships perished.** Another edition, saying “And they corrupted a third of the ships,” signifies that the third which died killed another third—that is, the generation succeeding it—through harmful tradition and the imitation of an unprofitable doctrine.

**And a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, etc.** The heretics, whom the Apostle Jude calls stars of seduction, falling from the Church’s height, strive to infect the fountains of the divine Scriptures with the flame of their wickedness. They do not fear falsifying not only their meaning but often their very words. They are worthy of the name “Wormwood,” whose small admixture commonly makes a great sweetness bitter.

**And many people died from the waters.** For many, as the Apostle says, follow their lusts, through whom the way of truth is blasphemed (2 Pet. II). Nevertheless, according to Moses’ teaching, every wave of water is drinkable for the people of God.

**And a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, etc.** The Church’s splendor, shining like a star, is often darkened by false brothers, who, whether amid the prosperity or adversity of the world, make it shine less brightly through their defection.

**And a third of the day did not shine, and likewise of the night.** Another edition reads: “And a third of the day appeared, and likewise of the night.” That is, it was struck so that a third of the day and a third of the night might appear—what belongs to Christ and what belongs to the devil. It was struck for this purpose, that is, handed over to its own desires, so that, as sins overflowed and grew insolent, each might be revealed in its appointed time.

**And I saw and heard the voice of one eagle flying through the midst of heaven, etc.** The voice of this eagle flies daily through the mouths of the Church’s eminent teachers when they solemnly preach to lovers of the earth that the wickedness of heretics, the savagery of Antichrist, and the day of judgment will come upon them, saying: “In the last days perilous times will come, and people will be lovers of themselves” (2 Tim. III); and below: “People corrupted in mind, disapproved concerning the faith” (ibid.); and elsewhere: “Then the lawless one will be revealed, who opposes and exalts himself above everything called God or worshiped” (2 Thess. II). And again: “The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. When they say, ‘Peace and security,’ then sudden destruction will come upon them” (1 Thess. V).

**Concerning the remaining voices of the three angels.** This does not mean that the angels’ trumpets inflict plagues upon the world, but that each, in its own time, proclaims those that are coming or will come.

## CHAPTER IX

**And I saw a star fallen from heaven to the earth, etc.** He explains by what fuel the flame of the heretics, which he had mentioned briefly, was kindled. The ancient enemy, whom the Lord saw “like lightning falling from heaven” (Luke X), opened the hearts of his followers through a blasphemous doctrine and thoroughly taught them to seek high things like smoke and to speak iniquity on high.

[Col. 0157C] **And the smoke of the pit rose like the smoke of a great furnace, etc.** Heretical madness, a herald of the great furnace—that is, the final persecution—burns fiercely. It strives to obscure not only the weaker, who, like the air, touch in some fashion the boundaries of earth and heaven, but also the light of the exalted, though it cannot extinguish it. “If it were possible, even the elect will be led into error” (Matt. XXIV).

**And locusts came out of the smoke upon the earth.** Just as the saints are Christ’s body, members from a member, so also, attached members of the dragon’s flesh, some are born from others. The smoke of heretical blindness, issuing from the mouth, gives birth to the destructive pride of the wicked. Those shaken loose from arrogance do not, however, abandon earthly things. For the smoke from which they are born, although it seeks high things, always fails within itself.

**And power was given to them, etc.** Heretics are compared to hostile powers: apparently innocent in the face, but keeping poisons in their rear parts.

**And they were commanded not to harm the grass of the earth, nor anything green.** He shows that the locusts are human beings, who are sent not against grass but against human beings. Here we understand “grass” in the ordinary sense.

**Except only those people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.** Those are said to have the seal of God on their foreheads in whom it is possessed as it ought to be. Above, the angel who brought the seal of the living God from the rising of the sun described it as fixed and inviolable. Here he wished to use the kind of expression by which it is said: “No one says, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except in the Holy Spirit” (1 Cor. XII)—that is, perfectly and truly.

**And it was said to them that they should not kill them, etc.** Although heretics, supported by secular power, may be permitted temporarily to attack the good, they cannot kill the soul, as the Lord says. The period of five months signifies the time of this world, on account of the fivefold division of the senses that we use in this life. The fact that another translation contains six months accords with the same meaning because of the six ages of the world.

**And their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.** Just as a scorpion spreads its poison from behind, so the impiety of the wicked harms from behind when it compels people, through threats or flatteries, to prefer temporal things—which lie behind—to the eternal good that lies before them. This generation of vipers hands this scorpion on to its offspring, contrary to the Gospel parable.

[Col. 0158B] **And in those days people will seek death and will not find it.** They will prefer to bring miserable life to an end by a swift death. Thus blessed Cyprian complained that this had occurred during the persecution under Decius: “Those wishing to die,” he said, “were not permitted to be killed.”

**And the appearance of the locusts was like horses prepared for battle.** That is, they were like the final persecutors. In the final war, which he will describe through the following angel, he says that horses fight. Or, more simply: just as horses are driven into battle not by their own reason but by the impulse of the one who controls them, so evil teachers, driven by a demonic spirit, attack the Church.

**And upon their heads were what looked like crowns resembling gold.** The twenty-four elders, who are the Church, have golden crowns. These, however, fashion for themselves false triumphs of victory resembling gold in their foolishness.

**And their faces were like human faces, etc.** In the human face he marks the simulation of reason; in women’s hair, loose and effeminate behavior; in lions’ teeth, which customarily both tear and produce a natural stench, the ferocity of the mind and the ill repute of their teaching; and in iron breastplates, hearts hardened against the truth. They “have the appearance of godliness but deny its power” (2 Tim. III); they come “in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves” (Matt. VII).

**And the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horses’ chariots rushing into battle.** This is more to be feared than explained: such strength is added to this army. First the smoke rises. Then it produces locusts, which are compared first to scorpions and soon afterward to horses and lions. Their strength would already be sufficient, if they did not also come armored. Now, however, they are said to be winged and like combatants in chariots.

**And they had tails like scorpions, etc.** Just as a scorpion advances by touch but strikes with its tail, so the deceitful destruction of the wicked appears gentle and harmless in the face, but, while secretly killing, carries death as though concealed.

**They had power to harm people for six months.** This again signifies the present life, in which falsehood can prevail either for capturing the useless or for temporarily tormenting the spiritual.

**And they had over them as king the angel of the abyss.** Although God is supremely good, by hidden yet just judgments he permitted an angel suited to such beings to rule over them.

**The first woe has passed; behold, two more woes are still coming.** Since he had foretold that three woes were to come, he now recalls that one of them has already arrived in heretical deceit, while two remain. These will befall the perverse in the time of Antichrist and on the day of judgment.

**And the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, etc.** The sixth angel represents the preachers of the final conflict, who, admonished by the Gospel, expose the frauds of Antichrist. The horns of the golden altar are the Gospels, preeminent in the Church.

[Col. 0159B] **Release the four angels, etc.** He indicates how greatly the ancient enemy, with his attendants, will persecute the Church at the end of the world. Since the time of the Lord’s passion he has been confined in the hearts of the impious, restrained by divine power so that he cannot harm the Church as much as he wishes. The Euphrates, the river of Babylonia, indicates the power of the worldly kingdom and the floods of persecutors. This is the great mountain that he had foretold was cast, burning with fire, into the sea.

**And the four angels were released.** In the manner of prophecy, which shows us things that are to come, he sees in the spirit what has happened. He said four angels because that persecution will rage in the four regions of the world. These are the ones whom above he saw standing at the four corners of the earth and restrained from harming the earth and sea for the marking of God’s servants.

**Who had been prepared for the hour and day and month, etc.** The wicked spirits, who at every moment of the hours and seasons hunger for human death, are then permitted to rage more freely, at the appropriate time, for the testing of the Church and the destruction of those destined to perish. What do you think those who are released will do, when they do so much harm while bound?

**And the number of the cavalry was twice ten thousand times ten thousand.** This number signifies the deceitful duplicity of the perverse army. This can be more easily understood in another translation, which says “twice myriads of myriads.” The Gospel parable also sets this number against a king who has ten thousand (Matt. IV), as though the duplicity of the wicked resists the simple faith of Christ, whom thousands upon thousands serve and ten thousand times a hundred thousand attend (Dan. VII).

**And in the vision I saw the horses and those who sat upon them, etc.** The wicked spirits are clothed in the punishments of those over whose hearts they preside. For we read that those who worshiped the beast would be tormented with fire and sulfur, and that the smoke of their torments would rise forever and ever. Note that in the plague of the locusts he did not say that he saw riders, but only horses. Here the magnitude of the persecutions openly reveals the presence of the opposing power. Finally, here there are lions’ heads, whereas there faces are human but only the teeth are bestial. For heretics often display something human, but the ministers of the final calamity extort through punishments what they persuade by words and signs.

**And from their mouths came fire and smoke and sulfur.** He shows what he had called “hyacinth” in place of smoke. These things do not visibly proceed from their mouths; rather, through harmful preaching they generate punishment for themselves and for their hearers. “I will bring fire out from your midst,” he says, “and it will consume you” (Ezek. XXVIII).

**For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails.** That is, in speech and office. For the prophet who teaches falsehood is himself the tail. He conceals the blind and filthy part, so to speak, through the shifting movement of a flattering tongue, saying to the wicked: “You are good.”

**For their tails are like snakes, etc.** False teachers, resembling the ancient serpent who deceived the human being, supported by the patronage of rulers, do more harm than if they persuaded by speech alone. “He sits in ambush with the rich,” it says (Ps. X).

**And the rest of the people who were not killed by these plagues, etc.** Since he had described false Christians and heretics, he now, in order to encompass the entire body of the devil, also mentions the error of the pagans. It does them no good not to be killed by these plagues, since it is clear that they will then still persist in pagan wickedness. For in that persecution the pagans will not be compelled to consent to the things mentioned above; they will die in their own unbelief.

And they did not repent of their murders, etc. They add wicked practices to their impious religion. Having described the cruelty of the Antichrist, he now, in his customary manner, recapitulates the beginning of Christ’s birth and the glory of the Church, in order to show the Antichrist’s downfall.

## CHAPTER X

And I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven, clothed with a cloud. The angel of the Great Counsel descends from heaven, clothed in the cloud of the flesh. As Isaiah also says: “Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and enters Egypt” (Isaiah 19), “and a rainbow was upon his head.” The promise of propitiation, abiding toward the good.

And his face was like the sun, etc. With the Lord’s face shining—that is, with his knowledge made manifest through the glory of the resurrection—his feet, which were to evangelize and announce peace upon the mountains (Romans 10), are illumined by the fire of the Holy Spirit and made firm like a column. For James, Cephas, and John appeared to be columns of the Church.

And he had in his hand a little open book. This is the book mentioned above, which, closed beneath a long-lasting covering, the Lord’s grace at last opened, so that, according to the prophet, even the deaf might hear the words of the book (Isaiah 29). And rightly was his face like the sun, because he now carries the book open.

And he placed his right foot upon the sea, and his left upon the earth. The preaching of the Christian faith is spread over land and sea. Allegorically, however, the stronger members are stationed amid greater dangers, and the others amid dangers proportionate to their capacity. For God does not allow us to be tempted beyond what we are able to bear (1 Corinthians 10).

[Col. 0161A] And when he cried out, the seven thunders uttered their voices. While the Lord preaches with power, the Church also, filled with sevenfold grace, raises her voices for preaching. “The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken; who will not prophesy?” (Amos 3). The seven thunders, then, are the same as the seven trumpets about which he speaks.

And when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write. For earlier he heard: “What you see, write in a book” (Revelation 1).

The things that the seven thunders spoke, do not write them. The mysteries of the Christian faith are neither to be displayed indiscriminately to everyone, lest they become cheap, nor to be concealed from the worthy, lest they remain wholly hidden. For this reason he later heard: “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book” (Revelation 22). Both statements are included in a single verse in Daniel, to whom the angel says: “Seal the book and close the words until the appointed time” (Daniel 12).

[Col. 0161B] And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth raised his hand toward heaven and swore, etc. The angel swears by him who lives forever, while Christ, coming in the name of the Father, confirms by the unchangeable truth of his word: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away” (Matthew 24).

Who created heaven and the things that are in it, etc. Since he stands upon sea and earth and stretches his palm toward heaven, he appropriately swears by the Creator of heaven, earth, and sea.

Because there will no longer be time. There will indeed be, as the psalm says, “the time of the wicked forever” (Psalm 80); but the changing variety of worldly times will cease at the last trumpet. “For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, and their inheritance will be everlasting” (1 Corinthians 15).

The mystery of God will be consummated, etc. The mystery now proclaimed in the Gospel will then be consummated, when “the wicked will go into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into everlasting life” (Matthew 25).

And the voice that I heard from heaven speaking to me again, etc. As the Lord reveals the mysteries of the future and says, “For the kingdom of heaven has drawn near” (Matthew 10), the Church too is instructed to receive the same book for preaching. These words may also appropriately refer to John himself, when he would return from exile to preach.

[Col. 0161D] And I went to the angel, saying that he should give me the book. Let whoever wishes to receive the mysteries of teaching approach the Lord.

And he said to me: Take the book and devour it. That is, implant it in your inward parts and inscribe it upon the breadth of your heart.

And it will make your belly bitter, etc. When you have received it, you will delight in the sweetness of divine speech, but you will feel bitterness when you begin to preach and practice what you have understood. Or certainly it is to be understood according to Ezekiel, who, after saying that he had devoured the book, added: “And I went away bitter, in the indignation of my spirit.”

And he said to me: You must prophesy again concerning peoples and nations. He explains what the devoured book and the sweetness mixed with bitterness signify: namely, that, rescued from exile, he would preach the Gospel to the nations—sweet through love, but bitter because of the persecutions that had to be endured.

## CHAPTER XI

And a reed like a rod was given to me. In the reed he received the ministry of writing the Gospel. It is not empty and superfluous in its vain brilliance, but is like the rod of righteousness, the rod of God’s kingdom (Hebrews 1). For he describes Christ’s eternal kingdom.

Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar. “Rise” was said, not because John heard these things while sitting, but because by this word the hearts of individuals are roused to measure the evangelical Scripture and their conduct. For there they discover how far each person is progressing and how closely each agrees with the divine rule.

And those who worship in it. Since not all who appear to belong to it worship in it, just as in the words, “Whoever confesses me,” he commands that one part not be counted, saying:

But the court that is outside the temple, cast out, etc. Those who are joined to the Church in name only and approach neither the altar nor the Holy of Holies are cast out from the rule of the Gospel and joined to the nations. For “all the glory of the king’s daughter is within” (Psalm 45).

And they will trample the holy city for forty-two months. They are not only expelled from the Church, but also attack that same Church together with the allied nations for three and a half years. This does not mean that they trample it only during that period—that is, the time of the Antichrist—but that the whole body of evildoers belongs, as it were, to that one as its own head, in those among whom the working of iniquity is already active.

[Col. 0162C] And I will grant to my two witnesses, etc. So that the cruelty of the wicked might not terrify the hearer, he recalls that the Church, united from two peoples, is also to be illumined by the grace of virtues. With her eyes always fixed upon her head, namely Christ teaching in the flesh, she is said to prophesy for three and a half years. The months of three and a half years—that is, forty-two months—amount to 1,260 days. Daniel, however, writes 1,290 days for the same period, during which the abomination is to be set up for desolation.

Clothed in sackcloth. That is, established in confession of sin. As the prophet says: “But when they troubled me, I clothed myself in sackcloth” (Psalm 35).

These are the two olive trees, etc. The Church, illumined by the light of the two Testaments, always stands ready to obey the Lord’s commands. The prophet Zechariah also saw a single seven-branched lampstand and these two olive trees—that is, the Testaments—pouring oil into the lampstand. This is the Church with her unfailing oil, which makes her burn as a light throughout the world.

And if anyone wishes to harm them, fire will come out of their mouths, etc. If anyone injures the Church, he is consumed by fire and condemned under the returning judgment of that very injury. For “all who take the sword will perish by the sword” (Matthew 26). Hence also the Chaldean flame that was brought against God’s children consumed the very ministers of impiety. [Col. 0163A] Or, in a good sense, the person is spiritually consumed by the fire of the Church’s prayers and changed for the better. “You will heap burning coals,” he says, “upon his head” (Romans 12).

These have power to shut heaven, so that it may not rain, etc. The Church in Christ has been given all power in heaven and on earth, with the keys for binding and loosing entrusted to her (Matthew 28). But heaven is also shut spiritually, so that it does not rain and the blessing from the Church does not descend upon the barren earth. As the Lord says concerning the Father of his vineyard: “I will command the clouds not to rain upon it” (Isaiah 5).

And they have power over the waters, etc. They not only hold back the waters, but also make those that have descended useless; this is what it means to turn the waters into blood. [Col. 0163B] For the good fragrance of Christ, wafting from the Church, is for some “the fragrance of death unto death,” and for others “the fragrance of life unto life” (2 Corinthians 2).

And when they have finished their testimony, the beast, etc. He plainly shows that all these things occur before the final persecution by saying, “When they have finished their testimony”—that testimony, certainly, which they bear until the revelation of the beast that is to emerge from the hearts of the wicked. This does not mean that they will not then rely upon the same testimony by resisting the enemy bravely, but that the Church is believed then to be deprived of the grace of virtues, while the adversary openly flashes forth signs of falsehood. For “want will go before his face,” as the Lord says (Job 41).

And he will conquer them and kill them. He will conquer in those who have succumbed; he will kill in those who have been slain with praiseworthy patience for Christ’s name. Or, if “he will conquer and kill” is understood spiritually, we shall take it as referring to part of the witnesses. As the Lord says in the Gospel: “They will hand you over to tribulation and will kill you” (Matthew 24). The evangelist Luke indicates that this was said in part when he says: “They will kill some of you” (Luke 11).

And their bodies will lie in the streets of the great city. “If they persecuted me,” he says, “they will also persecute you.” It is therefore no wonder if the city of the wicked, which did not fear crucifying the Lord, also holds his servants, even when killed, up to mockery. Ecclesiastical history often reports such events.

Which is spiritually called Sodom, etc. That is, mute and dark, possessing neither the light of faith nor the voice of confession. For “with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10). These provinces were visibly struck as a sign of spiritual punishment by these plagues: consuming fire and water turned into blood.

And people from the peoples and tribes will see, etc. He did not say, “The peoples and tribes will see,” but “many from the peoples”—those who, while others believe, openly ridicule the holy ones.

And they will not allow their bodies to be placed in tombs. He described their desire and their opposition, not their ability to prevent the Church from existing in memory. As in the words, “You neither enter yourselves nor allow others to enter” (Matthew 23), although others enter while they oppose them. They will act openly concerning the bodies both of the living and of the slain: they will neither allow the living to be gathered together in remembrance by celebrating sacred rites, nor allow the slain to be mentioned in remembrance, nor allow their bodies to be buried in remembrance of God’s witnesses.

[Col. 0164A] And those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them. Whenever the righteous are afflicted, the unrighteous rejoice and feast, just as, while the wicked man exalts himself, the poor man is set ablaze.

Because these two prophets tormented them. On account of the plagues by which the human race is afflicted because of the Testaments of God, even the sight of the righteous weighs upon the unrighteous. As they themselves say: “He is burdensome for us even to look upon” (Wisdom 2).

And after three and a half days, the spirit of life from God, etc. Up to this point the angel narrated what would happen; now he introduces the event he hears is to occur: after the kingdom of the Antichrist has been destroyed, the saints have risen to glory.

[Col. 0164B] And great fear fell upon those who saw them. He spoke of all the living, because the righteous survivors too will be terrified at the resurrection of those who had been sleeping.

And they ascended into heaven in a cloud. This is what the Apostle said: “We shall be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air” (1 Thessalonians 4).

And their enemies saw them. Here he separated the unrighteous from those whom he had said collectively were afraid.

And in that hour there was a great earthquake, etc. As the terror of judgment presses upon them, the entire city of the devil, built upon sand, will collapse together with all its builders. For ten and seven are both perfect numbers. If this were not so, the whole would have to be understood from a part.

And the rest were thrown into fear. Who among human beings “will boast that he has a pure heart,” when the powers of heaven are shaken?

And they gave glory to the God of heaven. These are those built upon the rock who, while others fall in the earthquake, glorify the Lord by a right confession from their own firm foundation. For “the righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance of the wicked.”

Some interpret the two prophets as Enoch and Elijah. Preaching for three and a half years, they will strengthen the hearts of the faithful against the faithlessness of the Antichrist that will soon follow. After they have been killed, his cruelty will rage for an equal period; finally, when the struggle has been renewed, he will be overcome by the saints who were believed to be dead, as though protected in hiding places. These prophets are said to rise because they form one body; and when those whom people already thought dead are seen, the persecution will be intensified, so that many of those considered worthy of either the number seven or the number ten will fall. Daniel says: “He will confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in half a week sacrifice and offering will cease, and there will be the abomination of desolation in the temple” (Daniel 9). And later: “And when the abomination has been set up for desolation, there will be 1,290 days” (Daniel 12). This number varies around the course of three years and six months. Finally, Elijah once destroyed his adversaries with fire; after hiding for three and a half years, he held back the rains; and, after killing the false prophets, he turned Israel back to the Lord through the sacrifice that had been taken away.

[Col. 0165A] The second woe has passed, and behold, the third woe will come quickly. This second woe refers not to a recapitulation, but to the battle of the horses, which was stirred up by the trumpet of the sixth angel. The eagle had foretold three woes to come from the sound of three trumpets. But at that point he did not say this, lest it be thought that the third would immediately follow—the third that belongs to the seventh angel and to the end.

And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, etc. The first six trumpets, compared with the ages of the present world, announced various encounters of the Church in war. The seventh, however, announcing the eternal Sabbath, indicates only the victory and dominion of the true king.

And the twenty-four elders worshiped God, etc. “Behold,” he says, “the third woe will come at the sound of the seventh angel.” And when he had sounded, he mentioned only the Church praising God and giving thanks. Hence we understand that the recompense of the good is nothing other than the woe of the wicked.

Who are and who were, etc. Although the wicked rebel, you have reigned from the beginning; but now their fury, crushed under your judgment, will perish. For “the Lord has reigned; let the peoples rage” (Psalm 99).

And the time for the dead to be judged and to give their reward, etc. This agrees with the order of the Gospel reading: first all nations are to be gathered before the Judge; then those on the right are to be placed in the kingdom of the Father, with its many dwelling places; but the wicked, driven beyond the boundaries of the kingdom, are to be scorched by the flames of the curse.

And to destroy those who corrupted the earth. This is the final woe. Up to this point he has spoken of the seven angels sounding their trumpets; now he recapitulates from the Lord’s birth, intending to describe the same events differently and more fully.

And the temple of God in heaven was opened, etc. Once the Lord’s temple, placed on earth, concealed the ark of the covenant closed beneath a mystical veil. Now, however, in the Church—which is the temple of the living God, whose citizenship is in heaven (Philippians 3)—the veil of the former temple and the intervening wall of the enclosure having been torn apart by the Lord’s blood, the ark of his Incarnation is now revealed to the whole world. For, as it were, heavenly manna in pure gold, divinity is present in a holy body.

And there were flashes of lightning and voices, etc. All these are manifestations of the Church’s radiance, preaching, and wars. He had said that these things also occurred in the description of the preaching of the seven angels from the Lord’s coming, when he stood upon the altar, but there he spoke generally from beginning to end. Then he described in separate parts how these things occurred; so now also, saying that the temple of God in heaven had been opened and that battles followed:

## CHAPTER XII

And a great sign appeared in heaven. This is also now apparent in the Church: God becoming human.

A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet. The Church, surrounded by Christ’s light, tramples upon temporal glory: “In his days righteousness will arise, and an abundance of peace, until the moon is lifted up or destroyed” (Psalm 72). That is, the abundance of peace will increase until it consumes all mutability of mortality, when death, the last enemy, is destroyed (1 Corinthians 15). Or because the same Church partly enjoys Christ, the sun, in heaven, and partly journeys in the body away from the Lord. Here one may understand what is said: “His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me” (Song of Songs 8).

Upon her head a crown of twelve stars. The Church’s head is adorned with the twelvefold number of the apostles, whether you understand “Christ” or designate by the name “head” the very beginning of that Church as it was being born. “You placed upon his head,” he says, “a crown of precious stone” (Psalm 21).

And she was pregnant, and she cried out in labor. Spiritually, the Church both gives birth to those whom she bears and does not cease bearing them again after they have been born. As she herself says: “My little children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you” (Galatians 4).

And she was suffering as she labored to give birth. Thus the Lord says in the Gospel: “When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the anguish because of her joy” (John 16). Explaining this to the disciples, he added: “So you also now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice” (ibid.).

And behold, a great red dragon, etc. The devil, blood-red with cruelty against the Church, is armed with the power of an earthly kingdom. By the seven heads he means all his kings, and by the ten horns his entire kingdom.

And its tail was dragging a third of the stars of heaven, etc. He indicates the strength and wickedness of the enemy, whom the Church, with the Lord’s help, conquers—the enemy who, through deceiving fraud, has cast down an innumerable portion of angels or human beings as though by a tail. For a tail is a blind and filthy part, concealing filth beneath its own covering so that it does not appear. Tychonius, in his customary manner, interprets the third of the stars that fell as false brothers, because the other third is the Church and the third is the external enemies.

And the dragon stood before the woman, so that when she had given birth, he might devour her child. The devil lies in wait for the Church, striving to extinguish Christ’s faith in the hearts of believers, so that the one whom she has brought forth by teaching, he may, as it were, kill after he has been taught. This plot was prefigured in Herod, who, like the internal enemies, pretended that he wished to worship the Lord in order to destroy him.

And she gave birth to a male child. Despite the dragon’s opposition, the Church always gives birth to Christ. He called him male because he is the conqueror of the devil, who had conquered the woman. For what child is there but a male? He “will rule all the nations with an iron rod” (Psalm 2): with inflexible justice he rules the good and crushes the wicked. This is also promised earlier to the Church: “I will give him authority over the nations, and he will rule them with an iron rod” (Revelation 2). For the Church also gives birth to the Church daily, ruling the world in Christ.

And her child was caught up to God, etc. Impiety cannot seize Christ spiritually as he is born in the minds of hearers, because he reigns with the Father in heaven—the same one who also raised us and made us sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ.

And the woman fled into the wilderness. The Church, living in hope of eternal things, rejoices in pilgrimage through the wilderness of the present age, having received power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and over all the strength of the red dragon. She is like the Israelite people, which, fed with heavenly bread in the wilderness, conquered the fiery serpents by looking upon the bronze serpent.

Where she has a place prepared by God. “Be for me,” she says, “a protecting God and a place of refuge, so that you may save me.”

So that they might feed her there for 1,260 days. This number of days, which makes three and a half years, encompasses the entire period of Christianity, because Christ, whose body this is, preached for that length of time in the flesh.

And a great battle took place in heaven. Michael and his angels, etc. Heaven signifies the Church, in which he says that Michael and his angels fight against the devil, because they contend according to God’s will by praying for the pilgrim Church and providing assistance. Daniel also said that he would come to the Church’s aid in the final and most severe tribulation; hence some think that the Antichrist is to be destroyed by him. They are called his angels in the same way that they are called our angels. The Lord says: “Their angels always see the face of my Father” (Matthew 18)—namely, the angels who are fellow citizens of those to whom they belong.

And the dragon fought, and his angels. The angels of Satan are to be understood not only as those who by nature and will resemble him, but also as human beings entangled in his snares.

And they did not prevail. That is, throughout the whole period.

Nor was their place found any longer in heaven. That is, among holy people, who, through his expulsion, have already been made heaven; once they believe, they do not receive him again after he has been expelled.

And that great dragon was thrown down to the earth. The ancient enemy, expelled from spiritual realms, is confined more tightly among earthly things. This is what it means to be hurled down from heaven and cast upon the earth. To him it is said: “You will eat earth all the days of your life” (Genesis 3). Upon this earth he is crushed beneath the feet of the saints, as it is written: “You will walk upon the asp and the basilisk.”

[Col. 0167D] Now salvation and power and the kingdom of our God have come, etc. It is clearly shown in which heaven these things occur. For we know that Christ’s victory brought salvation about in the Church. Concerning this he says: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (Matthew 28). He does not mean authority that he always possessed, but authority that, from the time he wished, he began to possess in the Church, as the head in its members.

Because the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down. The angels rejoice with their brothers over their salvation—that is, over the salvation of those who will be fellow citizens, but are now pilgrims.

Who accused them before our God day and night. He reproaches them both for using prosperity badly and for lacking patience in adversity.

[Col. 0168A] And they did not love their lives even unto death. They rightly despise their lives for Christ, since through Christ’s blood alone they have conquered the adversary.

Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Here the inhabitants of heaven are to be understood as both angels and holy human beings; it is fitting for both to rejoice in the Lord, since human beings are joined to the angels and the angels serve the human nature assumed by Christ.

Woe to the earth and the sea, because the devil has come down, etc. Just as he taught that joy awaits the redeemed, so he taught that lamentation awaits those who perish. Great woe threatens those whom the most wicked enemy, now enraged, possesses.

And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, etc. The devil attacks the Church with an inextricable cunning; the more he is cast down, the more fiercely he persecutes her.

[Col. 0168B] And the two wings of a great eagle were given to the woman, etc. Supported by the two Testaments and avoiding the tumultuous poisons of the world, the Church daily seeks the solitude of a tranquil and disciplined spirit through the inclination of her mind, singing joyfully: “Behold, I have fled far away and remained in solitude” (Psalm 55). Nor is there any contradiction in her seeking the wings of a dove there, while here she receives the wings of an eagle. For just as she is represented by the dove because of the gift of the Holy Spirit, so she is represented by the eagle because of her lofty flight and elevated vision, by which she sees God with a pure heart. Her youth will be renewed like that of the eagle.

Where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time. The whole time of the Church is indicated, already encompassed in the number of days mentioned above. For “a time” signifies one year, “times” two years, and “half a time” six months.

And the serpent poured from its mouth water like a river after the woman, etc. Water signifies the assault of persecutors. Hence it is said: “Perhaps they would have swallowed us like water” (Psalm 124). Thus the Church, raised up not only by the word of God but also driven onward by the force of persecutions, hastens to fly out of the world.

And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river. This holy earth is the Lord’s flesh, which, swallowing the death it had assumed and which had prevailed over it temporarily, taught us also to swallow death. The Church may also be understood, since through her admonitions and prayers the enemy’s snares are avoided.

[Col. 0168D] And the dragon grew angry with the woman, etc. Seeing that the persecutions could not continue because they were turned aside by the mouth of the holy earth, he armed himself more intensely to persist in the mystery of crime, by which he might continually lie in wait.

Those who keep the commandments of God, etc. To keep God’s commandments in the faith of Jesus Christ is to fight with the dragon and provoke him to battle. And thanks be to God, who has rendered the undertakings of the savage dragon ineffective. For behold, after attempting to extinguish the Lord born in the flesh, he is frustrated by his resurrection. Later, when striving to break the apostles’ confidence in teaching, he attempted to carry away from human affairs the woman—that is, the whole Church. But having attempted this also in vain, he now attacks individual generations of the faithful everywhere. Hence it follows:

[Col. 0169A] And he stood upon the sand of the sea. That is, upon the multitude of the people, which the wind drives away from the face of the earth. Without doubt, the same enemy takes his stand there, intending to stir up snares and wars; the antecedent of *illius* (“of that one”) is uncertain.

## CHAPTER XIII

And I saw a beast rising from the sea. The beast has different interpretations according to the places in which it appears. Here, therefore, it signifies the body of the devil arising from the people of the wicked. For this is the sea that above is understood as the abyss. Hence the dragon is also called king of all that are in the waters, and according to David its heads are crushed in the sea.

Having seven heads and ten horns, etc. [Col. 0169B] He shows that the seven heads are the same as the ten horns. He had said that the dragon wore seven diadems upon seven heads; now he says that the beast has ten diadems upon ten horns. Seven and ten, then, mean the same thing, just as Scripture says that one will receive “sevenfold” in this age. Another evangelist says “a hundredfold” (Matthew 19).

And upon its heads were names of blasphemy. They call their kings gods, both those who are dead and regarded as transferred to heaven and placed among the gods, and also the Augusti on earth, which is, as they wish it, a name of divinity. Elsewhere he says that the whole beast itself is full of names of blasphemy.

And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, etc. It resembles a leopard because of the diversity of nations, a bear because of wickedness and madness, and a lion because of bodily strength and the arrogance of its tongue. We read in Daniel that the kingdom of the Chaldeans was compared to a lioness, that of the Persians to a bear, and that of the Macedonians to a leopard.

And the dragon gave it his power. Thus the Apostle, speaking of the devil’s body: “Whose coming,” he says, “is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders for those who are perishing” (2 Thessalonians 2).

And I saw one of its heads as though slain unto death, etc. The Antichrist, belonging among the heads of the earthly kingdom, dares to present himself as one who, in imitation of our true head, has been slain and risen again, offering himself to be received in place of Christ, who truly accomplished this. The deceit of this invention is said to have been prefigured in Simon Magus.

And the whole earth marveled after it. He uses the genus for the species, saying that the beast is worshiped, whereas human beings on earth will worship the counterfeit head itself under the name of the truly slain and living head.

And they worshiped the dragon that gave authority to the beast. They claim to worship God, who gave authority to Christ.

And they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast? They say: “Who is like Christ? Or who can conquer him?”

And a mouth was given to it, speaking great things and blasphemies. “Who exalts himself,” he says, “above everything that is called God or that is worshiped” (2 Thessalonians 2).

And authority was given to it to act for forty-two months, etc. For before the three and a half years it does not blaspheme with an open mouth, but in the mystery of crime; after dissension has occurred and the man of sin has been revealed, it will be exposed. Then it will say, “I am the Christ” (Matthew 24); but now it says, “Here is the Christ,” and “There he is” (ibid.). “Against God” signifies against God.

To blaspheme his name and his tabernacle. The wicked will usurp for himself the dignity of God’s name and will also presume to call his own assembly a church.

And authority was given to it to make war with the saints, etc. The whole is expressed by a part. It can conquer when, under the violence of the time, even the elect are shaken, if that can happen. This will condemn the Jews, who, refusing to believe the truth, accepted falsehood.

And all who dwell on the earth worshiped it. He said “all,” but specified those who dwell on the earth. For he says: “Those who depart from you will be written in the earth” (Jeremiah 17).

Whose names have not been written in the Lamb’s book of life. It is just that those who serve the author of death should not be written in the book of life, and that those deceived by the beast’s pretended death should lack fellowship with the Lamb who took away the sins of the world. “The Lamb,” he says,

Who was slain from the foundation of the world. The Lamb, as Peter says, was “unblemished, foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but manifested in the last times” (1 Peter 1). Another edition has translated this as “the Lamb marked out from the foundation of the world.” It may also be understood through hyperbaton, so that the names of the saints are said to have been written in the book of life from the beginning.

If anyone has an ear to hear, let him hear. Whenever Scripture inserts this statement, it seeks an attentive hearer because of the obscurity of the matter. And lest the devil’s momentary kingdom be considered great, he anticipates human thoughts by saying: “If anyone leads into captivity, into captivity he will go”—that is, the devil and the beast, who now appears to capture the nations in his own nets, will himself soon be a captive together with his followers.

If anyone kills with the sword, he must be killed with the sword. The Lord Jesus will kill the one who now persecutes the Church either with carnal or spiritual death, by the breath of his mouth, and will destroy him by the manifestation of his coming.

Here is the patience and faith of the saints. He had promised that the murderer would be killed; but because no one is crowned unless he has competed lawfully, he now says that courage is necessary—an undaunted heart. Having first described the beast generally in hypocrisy and then blaspheming with an open mouth, he describes the same beast in the rulers alone, first in hypocrisy and then after its revelation.

And I saw another beast rising from the earth. He called it “another” with respect to its office; otherwise it is one and the same. What the sea is, however, is the earth, as Daniel testifies. When he saw four beasts rising from the sea, the angel said to him: “These four great beasts are four kingdoms that will rise from the earth” (Daniel 7).

And it had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon. It displays the lamb’s horns so that it may secretly inject the dragon’s poisons. Through the hypocrisy of holiness, it falsely claims that the singular wisdom and life which the Lord truly possessed are present in itself. Concerning this beast the Lord says: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves” (Matthew 7).

And it exercised all the authority of the first beast. The wretched disciples follow their master in everything.

And it made the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast. He shows the power of seduction: that it has enslaved both the body and the soul that dwells within it.

Whose mortal wound was healed. That is, it pretended to have conquered death by rising again. Scripture had said that he was not slain, but “as though slain,” just as it is said of the Jews: “They themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled.” The evangelist did not affirm that those utterly defiled people could have been polluted by entering the praetorium, nor that the Jews, conscious of such great crimes, truly feared being polluted; rather, he reported what they had pretended, as though affirming it.

And it performed great signs, so that it even made fire descend from heaven upon the earth. It placed the miracle of fire, as though the greatest of the others, in the foremost position, so that, because the Lord Christ gave his disciples the grace of virtues when the Holy Spirit came in fire, it too might deceive its followers through cunning, as though by a similar gift.

And it deceives those who dwell on the earth, etc. For his coming will be, as has been said, “according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders” (2 Thessalonians 2). It is usually debated whether they are called “signs and lying wonders” because he will deceive mortal senses through phantasms, so that he appears to do what he does not do; or because those very things, even if they are true wonders, will lead believers into falsehood, since they will not know the devil’s power and will think that such things could have been done only by divine power. The devil did not consume Job’s entire household and all his flocks through an illusion, but by real fire and a whirlwind. However these signs are called lying signs—whether for this reason or that—there is no doubt that this is the point at which the temptation will appear greater than all others: when the godly martyr subjects his body to torments and yet sees the adversary perform so many miracles before his eyes.

Saying to those who dwell on the earth that they should make an image of the beast, etc. That is, that they should be like it and make an image for it, as another edition says: “As having the wound of the sword and having lived.” That is, they claim in that falsehood to have died together with and risen again with the Antichrist, as though he should establish himself as God and mediator between them and his followers; for our Lord Jesus Christ does not have another mediator between himself and his own.

And it was granted to it to give spirit to the image of the beast. That is, to the people themselves who fulfilled this falsehood by making themselves the image of the beast, it pretended to give the spirit of truth.

And so that the image of the beast might speak. It will not merely deceive the wretched populace by a spirit feigned through fire, but will also make it capable of instructing others.

And he will cause those who have not worshiped the image of the beast to be killed. Not that image which they say is being made, but the one to whose likeness they fashion the people. Therefore he causes the image of the beast to worship the image [Col. 0172A] of the beast—that is, the people to worship the devil’s invention.

And he will cause all, small and great, etc. Not everyone without exception, as though the Gentiles too were included, but those who belong to this mystery.

To bear a mark on the right hand or on their foreheads. The mark is the mystery of iniquity, which hypocrites receive under Christ’s name, both in conduct and in profession.

And so that no one might be able to buy or sell. By mentioning selling and trading, he taught that just as the Church has handed down a symbol for our salvation, so they, in evil, confine themselves by such a definition that they are granted no license to trade or sell—like merchants carried on one ship, who are held together by a uniform sign.

[Col. 0172B] Except one who has the mark of the name of the beast, etc. That is, one who shares in his fraud. For the mark—that is, the sign—the name of the beast, and the number of his name are one and the same. For it is the number of a man, lest we think him, according to the opinion of some, either the devil or a demon, but one of human beings, in whom Satan in his entirety will dwell bodily. For he is the man of sin, the son of perdition.

Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding, etc. This number is said by the Greeks to be found in the name of “Titan,” that is, “giant,” in the following manner: Τ, 300; Ε, 5; Ι, 10; Τ, 300; Α, 1; Ν, 50. And this name, Antichrist, is thought to have been appropriated for himself as though he surpassed all in power, boasting that he himself is the one of whom it is written: “He rejoiced like a giant to run his course; his going forth is from the summit of heaven,” etc. (Psalm XVIII).

Primasius also gives another name containing the same number: Α, 1; Ν, 50; Τ, 300; Ε, 5; Μ, 40; Ο, 70; Σ, 200—which signifies “contrary to honor.” Likewise the word Α, 1; Ρ, 100; Ν, 50; Ο, 70; Υ, 400; Μ, 40; Ε, 5—that is, “I deny.” Through these, both the character of the person and the harshness of the Antichrist’s work are intimated. Yet this requires an elaborate explanation: how could so great a seeker of praise wish to be marked by such a sign?

Who does not know, alternatively, that the number six, by which the world was made, signifies the perfection of a work? Whether simple, or multiplied by ten or a hundred, it displays the fruit of that same perfection—sixtieth and hundredfold. Now the weight of gold brought to Solomon each year was six hundred and sixty-six talents. Therefore, what is rightly both owed and paid as a gift to the true king, that deceiver and tyrant will also presume to demand for himself.

## CHAPTER XIV

And I saw, and behold, a Lamb was standing on Mount Zion. That is, the Lord Jesus Christ was supplying his Church, wearied beneath the burden of its contests, with an example of virtue and the protection of his defense. By displaying the body that has both been confounded by the dragon’s power and marked by cautery, lest you fear that the Lamb’s body had succumbed to the beast’s fury, he showed the Church rejoicing in its customary splendor and number. And he marked the beast as standing on the sand of the sea, but the Lamb as standing on Mount Zion.

[Col. 0173A] And with him were one hundred and forty-four thousand. This finite number should be understood as standing for the infinite, and, through the secret significance of its mystery, as suited to the company of virgins: those who love God with all their heart, all their soul, and all their mind (Matthew XXII), and whose body also, constituted from four qualities, is consecrated to him in integrity. For three times three is nine, and four times four is sixteen. Sixteen times nine makes one hundred and forty-four. Thus, when so perfect a multitude is seen with the Lamb on Mount Zion—those who, established in the merit of carnal life, are seen there—there should be no doubt about the remaining members of the Church.

Having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads. He shows what the imitation of the mark on the forehead of the beast’s body is, when he says that God and Christ are written on the foreheads of the Church.

And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters. Great is the voice of the saints, and great is the devotion of the love which, he says, he heard from heaven, when he declared that those who uttered the voice were standing on Mount Zion. He thus shows that by Mount Zion he meant nothing other than the Church, which, raised up by the exalted joy of contemplation to overcome the burdens of oppression, celebrates the contests of its King both with praise and with imitation. For this is truly to sing psalms to the Lamb who stands.

And the voice that I heard was like that of harpists harping on their harps. Since all the saints are God’s harpists, crucifying their flesh with its vices and desires (Galatians V), and praising him with psaltery and harp (Psalm CL), how much more are those who, by the privilege of evangelical chastity, make themselves wholly a holocaust for the Lord, singularly denying themselves and taking up their cross (Luke IX), following the Lamb wherever he goes (Revelation XIV)!

And they were singing as though a new song before the throne. The old song was: “Blessed is the one who has a seat in Zion and members of his household in Jerusalem.” But the new song is: “Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear” (Galatians IV). And again: “I will give,” says the Lord, “to eunuchs in my house and within my walls a place and a name better than sons and daughters” (Isaiah LVI).

And no one could sing the song except, etc. To sing the song to the Lamb uniquely means to rejoice with him forever, above all the faithful, even in the incorruption of the flesh. Yet the other elect can hear the song, although they cannot sing it, because through love they rejoice in the exalted state of those others, although they do not rise to their rewards.

For they are virgins, etc. Blessed Augustine beautifully explained this while admonishing virgins:

“Go forward,” he says, “holy boys and girls of God, men and women, celibate and unmarried; go forward perseveringly to the end. Praise the Lord more sweetly, whom you contemplate more abundantly. Hope more happily in him whom you serve more earnestly. Love more ardently him in whom you are more attentive to please. With your loins girded and your lamps burning, await the Lord when he comes from the wedding feast. You will bring to the Lamb’s wedding feast the new song that you will sing on your harps—a song of such a kind that no one will be able to sing it except you. For one especially beloved by the Lamb, who was accustomed to recline upon his breast, saw you in the Apocalypse: twelve times twelve thousand holy harpists, with undefiled virginity in body and inviolate truth in heart. Follow the Lamb, because the Lamb’s flesh too is surely virgin. Follow him in virginity of heart and flesh wherever he goes. For what is ‘to follow’ except ‘to imitate’? For Christ suffered for us, leaving you an example so that you might follow his footsteps” (1 Peter II).

These have been purchased from among all peoples as first fruits for God and the Lamb. From that holy and immaculate flock of the Church, they are chosen by the Holy Spirit as holier and purer offerings, according to the merits of their will. Concerning them, the Apostle, having no command from the Lord (1 Corinthians VII), entreats them to present their bodies as a living, holy, and pleasing sacrifice to God (Romans XII).

And no deceit was found in their mouth. Virgins are not joined to the divine company solely on account of the merit of chastity, unless they have also lived an immaculate life, free from every pollution of sin. Tychonius interprets this vision not specifically of virgins, but generally of the whole Church, which the Apostle betrothed to one man, to present a chaste virgin to Christ (2 Corinthians XI). He concludes as follows:

“He did not say, ‘Deceit was not in their mouth,’ but ‘was not found.’ As the Apostle says: ‘And such were some of you, but you were washed’ (1 Corinthians VI). And ‘the iniquity of the wicked will not harm him on the day when he turns from his iniquity’ (Ezekiel XXXIII), and he may be a virgin, and deceit may not be found in his mouth. For he calls virgins chaste and modest.”

And I saw another angel flying through mid-heaven, having an eternal gospel. Since he had described the Church, wandering in this world, as engaged in an uncertain and varied struggle with the dragon, it remains to repay each army with a fitting reward and to show what punishments follow the wicked and what rewards follow the good. Therefore the preacher, moving through the midst of the Church, carries the gospel of the eternal kingdom.

To evangelize those sitting upon the earth. It is fitting that those who are raised by heavenly flight should also lift earthly minds from the seat of their sluggishness through preaching.

And over every nation, etc. “This gospel,” he says, “will be preached throughout the whole world, and then the consummation will come.”

Fear God and give him honor, etc. “Take all the more care,” he says, “for your salvation, the sooner retribution awaits you—a retribution that cannot be changed forever—fearing the Lord, maker of the world, and not the beast’s temporal tyranny.”

And another angel followed, saying: Babylon that great city has fallen, has fallen. He says that the ruined city of the devil has already fallen—either according to the customary usage of Scripture, which often puts in the past tense what it knows will inevitably be fulfilled, or because the proud were then cast down by the Lord when they were inflated by the devil, as the Psalmist says: “You cast them down while they were being raised up” (Psalm LXXII).

[Col. 0175A] She who made all the nations drink from the wine of the wrath of her fornication. The city of the ungodly, gathered from all nations, intoxicates the nations themselves—that is, its own members—with the wine of error. But the city of the Lord, cultivating the vine of Sorek, does not wish to become drunk with the wine in which there is debauchery (Ephesians V), lest it be deprived of the promised denarius of life.

And the third angel: If anyone worships the beast and his image. That is, the devil and the slain calf’s head.

And receives the mark on his forehead, etc. By saying “on the forehead or on the hand,” he signifies that the devil marks some by an ungodly profession, but others only by their conduct.

And he too will drink of the wine of God’s wrath, etc. By saying, “He too will drink,” he shows that there is another who will drink, lest he exclude the one who, although he is not visibly mingled with the Gentiles, nevertheless worships the same beast under Christ’s name. Justly, however, those who offer the cup of the wrath of fornication are laid low by the Lord’s cup—not, as in Jeremiah, so that they may vomit out the wickedness of their hearts and be cleansed, but so that, condemned, they may perish in eternal death, stupefied.

And he will be tormented with fire and sulphur, etc. The saints reigning with the Lord can always see the punishment of the wicked, so that, giving greater thanks to their Deliverer for this, they may sing the Lord’s mercies forever. For the torments of the wicked, seen by those who agree with the just Judge, do not grieve them, just as the sight of Lazarus at rest could not refresh the rich man buried in flames.

And they have no rest day or night, etc. They say that a lion spares a prostrate man, but this beast, fiercer than a lion, inflicts greater punishments the more it is worshiped.

And if anyone receives the mark of his name. Saint Augustine interprets the beast as the impious city, its image as the semblance of a bird—that is, Christians under a deceptive image—and the mark as the sign of crime, saying that it is worshiped, submitted to, and assented to.

Here is the endurance of the saints. Although the beast has raged, temporal suffering—which is to be rewarded with eternal blessedness—does not distress the saints. On the contrary, they will see their persecutors, who now exult in temporal pride, enduring eternal punishments with the beast.

And I heard a voice from heaven saying: Write. A beautiful harmony now appears among the preachers. One proclaims that the Lord’s kingdom is coming; another, that the city of the devil has fallen; this one proclaims the flames of the wicked, another the rest of the blessed. He sends forth his voice from heaven and commands that it be committed to writing for eternal remembrance. For the righteous rejoice because their names are written in heaven, while the wicked are erased from the book of the living.

Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. I give you thanks, Jesus, who bless in heaven those who die in you on earth—how much more those who gladly lay down their lives both in your faith and for your faith!

From now on, says the Spirit, so that they may rest from their labors, etc. Just as he had said that the wicked have no rest forever, so conversely he teaches that the faithful, aided by their former works, rest from now on—that is, from the time of death. “When he gives sleep to his beloved, this is the Lord’s inheritance” (Psalm CXXVI). But because of the cold the lazy man refused to plow; therefore he will beg in summer, and it will not be given to him.

And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, etc. Having already announced what precedes through the voice of the heralds, it now remains to display the person of the Judge himself. Coming to judgment, he overshadows the glory of his divinity with the cloud of flesh, so that the wicked may see the one whom they pierced (John XIX).

Having on his head a golden crown. He described the nature of this crown earlier in the woman’s adornment: “And on her head a crown of twelve stars” (Revelation XII). Yet it can also signify the victory of the one who reigns.

And in his hand a sharp sickle. That is, the judicial sentence of separation, which cannot in any way be avoided. We are within it, however much we may try to flee. For whatever is enclosed within a sickle falls inside it.
